newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-INDIA BOWLED OUT FOR 210 AFTER LATE COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BOWLED OUT FOR 210 AFTER LATE COLLAPSE.

text.p: India were bowled out for 210 on the first day of their three-day match against Barbados on Saturday after collapsing in the final session.
India, 126 for three at tea, lost seven wickets for their last 84 runs in the last session after losing the toss and being put in to bat.
Leg-spinner Dave Marshall was the scourge of the Indian batsman, taking six wickets -- five of them after tea -- for 62 runs.

Opener Ajay Jadeja, who did not play in the first two test matches against the West Indies, provided the only real bright note for the touring Indians, scoring 50 before being caught by Stanton Proverbs off Ottis Gibson. Jadeja's innings lasted 223 minutes in which he faced 154 balls and struck 10 fours.
Jadeja and Vangipurappu Laxman put on 88 for the first wicket before Laxman was caught for 36 by Hendy Bryan at mid-off from Marshall's bowling immediately after lunch.

Fast bowler Bryan removed Rahul Dravid (19) who edged a lifting delivery to wicketkeeper Courtney Browne with the score on 115. Then Jadeja edged Gibson to Proverbs at first slip without any runs being added.
In the final session, Marshall claimed the wickets of Saba Karim (12), N.David (4), Sunil Joshi (4), Dodanarsiah Ganesh (0) and Abey Kuruvilla (11)
Bryan took the wicket of Saurav Ganguly for ten and Robin Singh fell to Gibson for the same score.
Navjot Sidhu, who made a double century in the second test last week, came in halfway down the order and was the not out batsman on 32.
India have so far drawn all their games on the tour -- the two test matches and a four-day match against Jamaica.
